name: Neo-Confederates
summary: Neo-Confederates defend the Confederate cause and the legality of secession, hold that the South is a distinct Christian civilization, and favor states' rights, limited government and free-market economics. The movement arose in reaction to desegregation and is described by historians as continuing the Lost Cause narrative; its most political wing, the League of the South, seeks an independent Southern republic with Anglo-Celtic cultural dominance, while heritage groups such as the Sons of Confederate Veterans emphasize memory and vindication.
scope: Modern neo-Confederate movement since the 1950s, centered on the League of the South (founded 1994) and the Lost Cause tradition, plus the libertarian-leaning Lincoln-critic writers (DiLorenzo, Kennedy brothers). Heritage-only groups disclaim the League's racial and theocratic aims, so race and theocracy answers are lower-confidence. Excludes the historical Confederacy itself and Southern Democratic politics generally.

sources.usedFor: Core tenets of the Lost Cause narrative and scholarly views.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Neo-Confederates favor limited government, much lower taxes and little state regulation, so a federal healthcare guarantee runs against the core program.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The League of the South opposes most state regulation of business, which a mandated wage floor would be.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Most neo-Confederates favor free-market policy, and the libertarian wing around the Mises Institute is influential in the movement.

public-ownership.rationale: Free-market and anti-statist economics is the documented mainstream; state ownership of industry is opposed.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The League opposes personal income taxes, favoring sales taxes and user fees, which excludes higher taxes on the rich.

unions-good.rationale: Not a documented issue; inferred from pro-market, anti-regulation economics and the Southern right-to-work tradition.

property-fundamental.rationale: Opposition to property taxes and regulation reflects a strong view of property rights, though the League itself is not a pure property-rights movement.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The League opposes most state regulation of business, so tighter corporate regulation is disfavored.

cut-welfare.rationale: Low taxation and minimal-state views imply welfare cuts, though the movement spends little time on welfare as such.

worker-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from free-market views, with a minority distributist or socialist-Confederacy strand.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from deep distrust of the federal government, which the League calls the Empire.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's Christian traditionalism pulls against legalization while libertarians pull toward it.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The movement sees speech restrictions as federal tyranny, and its leading groups are themselves targeted as hate groups; Hill openly embraces racist labels.

strong-leader.rationale: Neo-Confederate writing treats Lincoln as the model of a despot who bypassed constitutional limits, so executive bypass is distrusted.

state-harmful.rationale: They want a smaller and decentralized state, and some want an extreme laissez-faire minimum, but they seek their own Southern state rather than none.

limit-guns.rationale: The League opposes any regulation of firearms.

empower-police-military.rationale: The League opposes standing armies yet favors order and armed local forces; adherents are split and the issue is not central.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Movement culture is explicitly Christian and traditionalist on morals.

decide-locally.rationale: Decentralized federalism and strong states' rights are core political values; the League seeks a confederation of sovereign states.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from conservative law-and-order Southern traditionalism.

traditional-family.rationale: The League opposes whatever undermines marriage and the family and has rallied for traditional marriage.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: League rallies promoted traditional marriage and Hill embraced homophobia among his stated positions.

abortion-legal.rationale: The League describes Southern culture as Christian and anti-abortion.

more-religion-public.rationale: Neo-Confederates promote public Christian displays such as Ten Commandments monuments and crosses.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The movement arose partly in reaction to civil rights and portrays Reconstruction and its enfranchisement of Black Americans as wrong.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from traditional-family and Christian conservatism.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Adherents see Southerners as a distinct civilization and stress preserving Southern culture, flags and memory.

gradual-change.rationale: Mainstream groups favor orderly, nonviolent separation, but separation itself is a radical break with the existing order.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The League favors strictly limited immigration and campaigns against Southern demographic displacement.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Sovereignty-centered, anti-federal and Southern-nationalist; supranational authority is opposed.

free-trade.rationale: DiLorenzo praises the Confederacy's free-trade tariff and blames Northern protectionism, though the movement does not center the issue.

nation-first.rationale: Southern independence and sovereignty come first, with end-of-empire and anti-alliance leanings.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred from opposition to the empire and standing armies.

open-borders.rationale: Strict immigration limits and demographic-displacement rhetoric rule this out.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from pro-market economics.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from anti-regulation, anti-federal economics.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The movement is not organized around technology and holds no clear view.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from pro-market, pro-energy-production Southern conservatism.

revolution-justified.rationale: Secession is defended as a justified separation and some groups prepare for collapse of the US, but most favor an orderly rather than violent course.

experts-over-public.rationale: Adherents distrust universities and mainstream historians; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Free-market economics is the documented majority position.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred from private-property free-market views; a small minority claims the Confederacy was socialist.

land-value-tax.rationale: The League opposes property taxes, which this would greatly expand.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from opposition to income and property taxes.

basic-income.rationale: Inconsistent with low taxes and cutting welfare dependency.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: DiLorenzo presents protective tariffs as the Northern device that plundered the South.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Opposed by the League's rejection of state business regulation and central banking.

widespread-small-property.rationale: A minority distributist and agrarian strand favors it; not a mainstream tenet.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Contrary to every strand of the movement's economics.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The League opposes central banking and fiat currency.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not a Southern-nationalist program; inferred from free-market positions.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The League seeks a Southern republic, not a monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: Hill favors a kith-and-kin order and a hierarchical society over universal democratic rights; mainstream heritage groups are not anti-democratic.

direct-votes.rationale: Not addressed; secessionists invoke popular consent but favor state-level authority.

workers-councils.rationale: Socialist structures contradict the movement's economics.

right-to-secede.rationale: Defending secession as legal and seeking Southern independence is the defining position.

natural-rulers.rationale: The League envisions a hierarchical society led by an Anglo-Celtic elite.

political-violence-never.rationale: Most groups say they prefer peaceful separation, but the League formed paramilitaries and celebrated Booth.

war-builds-character.rationale: Lost Cause tradition romanticizes Confederate soldiers' chivalry and sacrifice.

separate-church-state.rationale: They want Christianity prominent in public life, and the League seeks a Christian-oriented South.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: SPLC describes a Christian theocratic goal for the League; mainstream heritage groups favor Christian public culture short of this.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Only the extreme laissez-faire minority holds it; the League instead wants local authorities and armed militias.

military-superiority.rationale: The League opposes standing armies and empire, while Southern heritage culture honors the military.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The League wants a South ruled by white men with Anglo-Celtic cultural dominance.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Class-conflict theory is foreign to a movement that stresses regional and cultural identity and defends the antebellum order.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Opposed by free-market and hierarchical views.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from property-rights and Anglo-Celtic nationalism.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The League itself demanded reparations for the South, and rejects reparations-style claims against others.

civilizational-union.rationale: Their nationalism is Southern, not transnational.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The movement pairs free markets with Christian and communal values; stance is inferred.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Hill advocates a kith-and-kin system over an impersonal state wedded to the universal rights of man.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The sources show no position on nature's intrinsic value; agrarian and Christian stewardship traditions pull in different directions.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred from Christian traditionalism and pro-natalism.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The agrarian tradition romanticizes rural life, but the movement does not condemn industrial civilization.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from distrust of centralized power.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from deep suspicion of federal power.

restore-past-order.rationale: The movement is restorationist about Southern history and traditional Christian order, though it also pursues a future independent republic.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The movement is principle-driven (states' rights, constitutional argument); inferred.

direct-action.rationale: The League pursues cultural secession and some paramilitary action while others use ordinary politics.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources show no stated view on whether methods should mirror goals, so adherents split between orderly politics and harder tactics.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Entirely contrary to its agrarian but settled-society ideal.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxian exploitation theory is rejected by the pro-market majority.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Contrary to every strand of the movement.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Rejects Marxist theory of imperialism; blames the Northern state, not capitalism, for war.

taxation-theft.rationale: The League opposes income and property taxes and the libertarian wing treats taxation as coercion, but this is not a universal statement of the movement.

harm-principle.rationale: Christian traditionalists favor restricting conduct on moral grounds.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Hill prefers kith and kin to universal rights; adherents emphasize the Southern people as a collective.

conscription.rationale: The League opposes standing armies; inferred.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The movement's central strategy is exit by secession.

positive-liberty.rationale: Free-market, limited-government view of liberty as non-interference.

media-academia-power.rationale: Adherents call mainstream Civil War history false history imposed by institutions.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Open racists in the League assert it, but heritage groups avoid the claim; contested within the movement.

organic-representation.rationale: Hill's kith-and-kin political order favors communal rather than party-based representation; inferred.

national-rebirth.rationale: The League presents Southern independence as renewal after decline.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Aim is independence, though the League wants additional states joined to a Confederacy; opposes empire.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The League wants a republic of sovereign states, not lordship.

bound-labor.rationale: Hill has called slavery God-ordained, but a legally bound tenant class is not a modern program.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: They claim truth about the war is being suppressed rather than denying that truth exists.

universal-morality.rationale: Christian orientation implies moral truths, though they reject universal rights of man.

single-common-good.rationale: Neither source frames politics as pursuit of one rationally derived common good; the movement speaks of a Southern people's interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The League's leaders voice antisemitism, while many Southern conservatives are Christian Zionists; genuinely split.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: No source addresses diaspora return; the movement is not organized around this question, so the answer is a neutral placeholder.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is not part of Southern nationalism, since the South already speaks English; nothing to infer here.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Contrary to private property and market economics.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred from free-market and traditionalist views on schooling.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: They oppose fiat money and central banking and favor sound money.

economic-freedom.rationale: The libertarian-leaning mainstream links liberty to markets.

rule-by-example.rationale: Lost Cause cults of chivalrous leaders suggest sympathy, but no program.

national-self-determination.rationale: Southern people claim a right to their own independent republic.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The movement embraces a Christian foundation for culture.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from immigration restrictionism and welfare skepticism.

class-collaboration.rationale: Hierarchical paternalism rather than class struggle; inferred.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The movement exists largely to preserve Confederate heritage, memorials and cemeteries.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Traditional family and marriage emphasis implies distinct roles; the Lost Cause idealized Southern womanhood.

ban-interest.rationale: Mostly sound-money capitalists, not interest prohibitionists.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Neo-Confederate movement began as resistance to desegregation, but current mainstream groups disclaim legal segregation while League leaders want a white-dominated order; split.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from pro-market, anti-regulation Southern conservatism.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The League says outsiders may live in the South only if accepting Anglo-Celtic cultural dominance.

elite-replacement.rationale: The League campaigns on Southern demographic displacement; more extreme claims are not universal.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from attachment to US-style constitutional arrangements.

national-mission.rationale: The League is an anti-empire secessionist movement; inferred.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Rejects feminist theory in favor of traditional family order.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Neo-Confederates portray the federal government as a tyrannical empire and Washington elites as hostile to the South.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not addressed; Christian pro-life stance suggests opposition.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Limited government and, for some, a minimal laissez-faire state are core; the League also stresses morals.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The League has opposed interracial marriage, though heritage groups do not state this.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: League leaders favor hierarchy and Anglo-Celtic dominance; Christian equality of souls pulls the other way.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Southern-settled society is regarded as legitimate; inferred.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Decentralized federalism favors local diversity of law; inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The movement supports public Christian expression.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A socialist-state doctrine; the movement opposes state strengthening and any socialist state.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Secessionists argue legitimacy rests on the consent of the Southern people.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist export targets are not discussed, and DiLorenzo's free-trade praise pulls against them, so adherents are indifferent.

population-transfer.rationale: The League wants dominance not expulsion; inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Not the movement's rule; League leaders celebrate violence, and the libertarian wing is a minority.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Anti-federal groups themselves risk being outlawed under such a power.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The republican concept of non-domination is not used in the sources; adherents frame freedom as states' rights and non-interference.

separated-powers.rationale: Their confederation of states and constitutionalism favor checks on power.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing policy with no counterpart in Southern nationalist writing; adherents would neither champion nor oppose it.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from pro-natalist Christian outlook.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: League argues for Anglo-Celtic cultural dominance and campaigns on demographic displacement.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not addressed; strongly contrary to tradition.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: DiLorenzo-style writing condemns Lincoln's wartime suspensions of liberties as despotism.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Opposed to pooling of sovereignty, as with federal union itself.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Neo-Confederate critique of Lincoln as despotic executive suggests wariness.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Southern Protestant tradition is largely congregational or Presbyterian; inferred.

clerical-rule.rationale: SPLC reports a theocratic aim, but nothing implies rule by senior clerics specifically.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not addressed; free-speech vs traditionalism split.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall elections are not mentioned in the sources; this is a procedural matter on which the movement has no stated position.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The League opposes standing armies and empire.

people-in-arms.rationale: The League opposes standing armies and firearm regulation, favoring armed civilians.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Agrarian Southern tradition values rural life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: No source treats a nation split by an outside-drawn border as an issue; the Southern case is about separation, not reunification.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Distrust of universities as hostile to Southern history.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: They treat Southern Christian civilization as distinct and superior in its own heritage.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Hill's kith-and-kin politics implies descent-based membership.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not covered in the sources; adherents favor Christian public culture, but exemptions for minorities are not discussed.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from sound-money stance.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Aim is political independence with market economy continuing.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The sources do not discuss rewriting constitutions; the movement appeals to the existing US Constitution and its own sovereignty claims.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Contrary to its low-tax, nation-first views.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Neither source discusses nuclear arms; the League's hostility to standing armies and the movement's pro-military culture pull in opposite ways.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Method of choosing a head of state is not a stated issue; Southern republics would likely differ on it.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The sources never discuss land-for-peace bargains, and adherents' Southern territorial claims do not translate to this statement.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: They stress strong property rights, as in opposing property taxes.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A debate internal to the Marxist left; the movement takes no side beyond rejecting Soviet socialism wholesale.

collective-defense.rationale: The League opposes standing armies but a Confederation would imply mutual defense; split.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Lost Cause narrative treats Southern states as conquered and occupied in the Union's war and Reconstruction.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Contrary to its Christian public-life program.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Whether the head of state is a unifying nonpartisan symbol is not discussed; neo-Confederates focus on limiting executive power instead.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: DiLorenzo-style Lincoln criticism treats the invasion of the South to stop secession as unjust.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The League wants a confederation of sovereign states with broad autonomy.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Contrary to its republican Christian outlook.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The League opposes the income tax altogether, and would find a flat one preferable to a progressive one.

character-from-environment.rationale: Hereditarian racialist wing and Christian human-nature views oppose the blank slate; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The critique of Lincoln centers on a ruler overriding constitutional limits.

space-expansion.rationale: Space exploration is not mentioned in any source on the movement, so it holds no distinctive view.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Mixed regime theory does not appear in the sources, though the movement admires constitutional checks, so it stays neutral.

leader-cult.rationale: Not typical; they attack the cult of Lincoln.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court custody is not addressed in the sources; traditional-family views give no clear direction here.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A claim internal to Marxism-Leninism that the movement has no stake in, beyond opposing socialism entirely.

refugee-return.rationale: No source addresses return of expelled refugees; the movement's concerns are domestic and immigration restriction rather than return rights.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Not a documented aim; the League seeks independence rather than irredentism.

common-currency.rationale: Opposition to fiat money and supranational union.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Hill's kith-and-kin appeals might extend to other Europeans but nothing in sources defines it.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Autonomous minority cultural institutions are not discussed; the League's call for Anglo-Celtic dominance cuts against it but is not explicit on this model.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Whether persecuted minorities should stay and seek rights or emigrate is not discussed in the sources on neo-Confederates.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Rejects Marxist historical materialism and emphasizes cultural and moral causes.

no-bailouts.rationale: Opposed to central banking and state economic intervention.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Adherents oppose federal courts but also majority federal rule.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Contrary to its traditional gender views.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: League has formed paramilitaries but most groups prefer orderly separation.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Hierarchy and Anglo-Celtic elite are favored.

history-own-civilization.rationale: They fought textbook battles to teach Lost Cause history.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: League legal counsel argued Black people were better off under slavery, a paternalist argument; not stated as a general doctrine.

patriotic-education.rationale: Textbook campaigns for heritage; patriotic content aims at Southern loyalty.

public-money-creation.rationale: They oppose fiat currency and central banks.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not an issue for the movement, which opposes American empire rather than seeking influence in former territories.

delink-world-market.rationale: Delinking from rich countries is a dependency-theory idea; the movement's free-trade leanings in DiLorenzo's writing run against it.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Libertarian wing and the League's anti-regulation views support free association; also fits race views.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: They appeal to the US Constitution's limits on federal power and defend gun rights.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Nothing in the sources relates to colonial-era treaties dividing peoples; adherents hold no stated view.

elective-rulers.rationale: The League seeks a republic of sovereign states.

minority-veto.rationale: Nullification and state veto traditions exist, but individual veto is not stated.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Neo-Confederate writing justifies resistance to Lincoln as lawless despot.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Constitutional limits on every branch are favored.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal sentience is not discussed in the sources; Southern traditionalists are split between stewardship and indifference.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: League has pledged good will toward Southern blacks and paternalism fits; inferred.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Neo-Confederates hold that states' rights and tariffs, not slavery, drove secession; critics call this denial of the historical record.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Defending Confederate memorials, cemeteries and flags is central to the heritage groups' stated purpose.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Neo-Confederates blame media and academia for hostile bias against the South rather than for pacifying the masses; the structural claim is inferred as unshared.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The movement sees an overbearing federal government imposing its order by coercion and elite ideology, not a consent-based hegemony; inferred from its anti-federal stance.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory sits with left critiques of capitalism, while neo-Confederates favor free markets and tariff-free trade; inferred from that economics.

native-born-offices.rationale: The League favors Anglo-Celtic cultural dominance and tight immigration limits, but no source states a native-born office rule, and heritage groups would not back one.

party-own-road.rationale: The statement concerns communist parties and is outside the movement, which is anti-communist, so it is neutral.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Limited-government, free-market neo-Confederates distrust aid and favor self-reliance, though they rarely discuss foreign development; inferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The movement seeks Southern independence, not recovering lost territory from a neighbor; the Lost Cause concerns memory of a defeat, so an inference at low confidence.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The League wants Anglo-Celtic cultural dominance by settler descendants, which runs against indigenous political leadership; inferred.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The movement rejects mainstream postwar liberal orthodoxy and the League's far-right ties make it hostile to anti-fascism as a founding value; inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The movement is strongly anti-communist and its libertarian writers treat the centralizing state as the threat, so it likely accepts equating both; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not a movement concern; the League stresses traditional family roles and limited government programs, so adherents are split.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The movement has no stated view, and adherents with traditional-family views and libertarians would diverge.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The League holds the South is a distinct Christian civilization that should govern itself in its own republic; inferred from that claim.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Limited-government and constitutional-compact views oppose a political military role, though the League's paramilitary interest complicates it; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Paying for domestic work is a state program at odds with limited government, and the League stresses traditional family roles; inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the League of the South's emphasis on traditional Christian family and kin.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred: it favours Southern rule by chosen Anglo-Celtic leaders and no source backs examination-based office.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from its free-market, limited-government economics, which opposes state controls on who buys firms.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the League's traditional family and Christian-society stance.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred from its constitutional-compact, limited-government outlook, which favours fixed terms under set rules.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from its limited-government, free-market views and calls to cut welfare.

land-use-tenure.rationale: It holds that property is fundamental and rejects redistribution, so common ownership of land is opposed.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from its limited-government, constitutional views, which favour legislative control of the public purse.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from the League's aim of Anglo-Celtic cultural dominance in a Southern republic.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the League's kith-and-kin nationalism and its hostility to immigration.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: It rejects equal outcomes and racial remedies, treating discrimination as intentional treatment.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from its free-market economics and its view that consumer demand is a legitimate market outcome.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from its limited-government, non-interventionist stance and opposition to humanitarian intervention.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from its defence of states' sovereignty and the right to secede, which it would extend to alliances.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred: League of the South rhetoric attacks federal and Wall Street elites, though its free-market economics make it wary of regulating business money.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred: the League seeks Southern sovereignty and distrusts outside groups, but sources show no stance on foreign funding rules.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred: the League stresses Christian family and Anglo-Celtic cultural continuity and opposes immigration, which fits birth-rate incentives.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred: the League's kith-and-kin localism supports keeping Southern land in Southern hands, though its property-rights stance cuts the other way.

job-guarantee.rationale: The movement's free-market, limited-government economics rejects state employment schemes.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred: the movement rejects federal power and regards the Union's wars as aggression, so it doubts that spreading democracy brings peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Neo-Confederates hold that secession is legal and that the federal government has no automatic claim to obedience, though League theology also stresses order.

non-intervention.rationale: Neo-Confederate writers condemn Lincoln's use of force against the seceding states and favour non-interference by the central power.

industrial-unions.rationale: The League opposes most state regulation of business and favours free markets, so state-organised industry unions run against it.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred: the SPLC records conspiratorial claims about outside groups in League writing, but heritage groups disclaim them and adherents split.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The League stresses Christian marriage and the traditional family, so abolishing legal marriage is rejected.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred: limited-government libertarian strands favour transparency, but sources show no stated position.

local-production.rationale: Inferred: the League's agrarian and Southern-localist tradition favours regional production and exchange, though its free-trade writers favour open markets.

informal-organisation.rationale: Inferred: the League is a formal organisation seeking a Southern republic, and the movement runs through established groups such as the Sons of Confederate Veterans.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The movement rejects federal and international authority over the South and holds that states' sovereignty overrides outside law.

religious-nation.rationale: The League describes the South as a distinct Christian civilization and seeks a Christian-based republic, with kith-and-kin nationhood.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred: the League of the South seeks Southern independence and sovereignty and would reject submission and tribute to any outside power.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred: states-rights and secessionist principles favour keeping revenue within the state or region, as in DiLorenzo-style arguments on tariffs that drained the South.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred: private possessions are protected, but the statement is tied to common ownership of the means of production, which neo-Confederates reject.

defeat-communism.rationale: Neo-Confederates favour free markets and limited government and, as Southern conservatives, oppose communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred: a limited-government, free-market outlook favours private provision and opposes a publicly funded system with mandated provider mix.

religion-illusion.rationale: The League of the South holds the South to be a Christian civilization, so religion as an illusion is rejected.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred: neo-Confederates defend free-market capitalism, though they do not describe it as progressive in a Marxian sense.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: the League promotes traditional family and gender roles and market economics, so economic transformation for women is rejected.

socialized-care.rationale: The League of the South upholds traditional family and opposes state-run childcare as against limited government.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred: Southern cultural defence would not favour foreign terms, but purging words is not a documented neo-Confederate aim.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred: respect for treaties is not a neo-Confederate theme, and a nation-within-borders argument may cut against their own secessionist legal claims.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred: the League favours a decentralised Christian society with private property, not communal ownership, though localism and small self-governing communities appeal.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred: the League seeks Anglo-Celtic cultural dominance in its own region, not government-sponsored settlement into minority-majority areas.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Inferred: neo-Confederates reject communism but largely defend capitalism; a few Distributist-leaning writers favour a third course, so adherents are split.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred from the belief that the South is a distinct people with an inherited homeland, though movement texts do not frame it as a competing claim.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Mainstream neo-Confederates do not deny it, though a fringe in the League of the South has been linked to antisemitism.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The League of the South opposes homosexuality on Christian grounds, but heritage groups avoid the issue, so no clear majority view.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The movement stresses limited government and liberty against federal power, but the League also seeks cultural dominance.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The League of the South favours a Christian theocratic order, though heritage groups disclaim this.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred from its anti-imperial reading of the North's rule over the South and its stress on local self-government.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic-law question outside the movement's concerns.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: the movement relies on constitutional arguments rather than religious-law legitimacy.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on local and state sovereignty and hierarchical Southern tradition rather than direct democracy in workplaces and universities.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The movement rejects the premise that racism and class overlap as oppressions, defending Southern heritage against it.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The League of the South and heritage groups follow conservative Christian views on sex and gender.

assisted-dying.rationale: Conservative Christian pro-life positions are standard in the League of the South.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The movement sees itself firmly on the traditionalist right.

alienated-labor.rationale: Its free-market economics, drawn from Mises Institute writers, rejects Marxist critiques of capitalism.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The League treats the South as an Anglo-Celtic Christian civilisation and has been hostile to Islam and non-Western immigration.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The League of the South holds that authority rests on God's law and a Christian order.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred: a Christian-culture movement would oppose restricting religious expression in schools and government.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from its free-market, limited-regulation stance, which opposes new restrictions on contracts.

social-market-economy.rationale: It favours laissez-faire free-market economics, not a state-managed social market.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The movement honours Confederate soldiers and the military tradition of the South.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from free-market, anti-redistribution views that accept unequal outcomes.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred from a non-interventionist strand, as in the Mises Institute and Lincoln-critic writers, but not a settled doctrine.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred: they idealise a republic of sovereign states and elected office, not hereditary rule.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred from their free-market, limited-government economics, which favour private banking.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from their hostility to outside control and distrust of centralised power, though the issue is not addressed.

property-franchise.rationale: Inferred: Southern conservatives have historically supported such limits, but modern adherents rarely state it.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred: the movement defends traditional Christian family roles and rejects feminist theory.

reification.rationale: Inferred: free-market advocates see markets as voluntary exchange, not distortion.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred: they defend private property and a free market in media, though they distrust mainstream media.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred from their constitutional-compact, limited-government argument against federal overreach.

racial-franchise.rationale: The League seeks Anglo-Celtic cultural dominance in a Southern republic, but heritage groups disclaim racial aims, so this is contested.

online-participation.rationale: Never addressed by the movement; no basis to infer a position.

open-government-data.rationale: Never addressed; limited-government views give no clear answer.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred: the League is Christian-theocratic in tone, but no legal limit on interfaith marriage is documented.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred: no documented religious-minority boycott; the movement's targets are racial and cultural.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred from the League of the South's traditionalist, hierarchical and constitutionalist outlook favouring elected local government; the issue is not addressed.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The League of the South presents the South as a distinct orthodox Christian civilization and defends traditional doctrine against modernizing reinterpretation.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The movement's free-market, Austrian-influenced economics sees wealth as the fruit of liberty, and it fears state power, not concentrated wealth.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The League of the South promotes a traditional Christian Southern culture and opposes the gay rights agenda.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The League describes the South as a Christian civilization and seeks a Christian society.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Neo-Confederates favour order and traditional authority and the League has promoted a militia-style Southern defence force.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The League seeks Anglo-Celtic cultural dominance in an independent South, not power sharing among communities.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Limited-government and free-market views, together with a stress on church and local community, favour private and local help over federal programmes.

term-limits.rationale: Never addressed as a doctrine; inferred as split between distrust of career politicians and indifference to the issue.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from a traditionalist and hierarchical outlook; delegation of votes is not part of the movement's programme.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a focus on Southern heritage, secession and limited government rather than global risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The League promotes a traditional patriarchal Christian order, which excludes women from clerical authority.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The League's traditional Christian patriarchal model gives the husband headship of the household.

missingStatements.text: Slavery was not the main cause of the American Civil War.
missingStatements.rationale: Neo-Confederates hold that states' rights and tariffs, not slavery, drove secession; critics call this denial of the historical record.

missingStatements.text: Public memorials, monuments and flags honoring Confederate soldiers should be preserved.
missingStatements.rationale: Defending Confederate memorials, cemeteries and flags is central to the heritage groups' stated purpose.

missingStatements.text: The federal union is a compact of sovereign states, each of which may judge and resist federal overreach.
missingStatements.rationale: The League promotes a confederation of sovereign states and argues the states never surrendered sovereignty.

notes: Wings differ: heritage groups (SCV, UDC) stress memory and deny racial aims; the League of the South openly advocates white, Anglo-Celtic and Christian dominance. A minority are distributist or claim the Confederacy was socialist. Race, theocracy and antisemitism answers reflect the League wing only partly and are lower-confidence.
